thread:
alex: escalate from CS — customer on prod (mobile app) reports streaming responses cut off mid-event, then reconnects but missing chunks. started ~10:30 UTC, ~25% of streams affected. They see partial JSON bodies in client and EventSource reconnects repeatedly. Logs show write errors on our side.

maria: got it. can you paste the server-side logs and a minimal repro? which endpoint and which model?

alex: endpoint: POST /v1/streams/generate (hosted API), model: redwood-large-v1. Customer claims it happens when their network is poor (mobile carrier) or when they background the app. I reproduced locally by throttling the client. logs: 
```
2026-01-24T10:29:15.243Z runtime[worker-7]: stream-start request_id=req_abc123 client=acme-mobile
2026-01-24T10:29:18.512Z runtime[worker-7]: write 1024 bytes to socket (non-blocking) returned EAGAIN after 2 retries
2026-01-24T10:29:18.513Z runtime[worker-7]: socket write failed: EPIPE (Broken pipe) request_id=req_abc123
2026-01-24T10:29:18.513Z runtime[worker-7]: aborting stream, sent partial event
```
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' | pv -L 20
```
(reproduces: pv throttles the client read to 20 bytes/sec).

jin: EAGAIN/EPIPE indicates OS send buffer filled and peer reading slow — server attempted non-blocking write and got EAGAIN, then eventual EPIPE when tcp peer closed. We saw similar in last year's edge case with Cloudflare + gzip. Did you check proxies in front (CF, ALB, nginx) and whether gzip/chunking is enabled?

alex: customer is behind Cloudflare Spectrum + our ALB -> envoy -> runtime. We run gzip compression gateway-wide. In the throttled repro I also swapped to direct to runtime (bypassing envoy) and still saw EAGAIN but less frequent.

sam: two quick suspects: (1) proxy buffering + gzip means the proxy may buffer some bytes before sending; when client is slow the proxy holds data and our runtime still sees the socket stall. (2) Node/Go runtime handling of backpressure: if code ignores write() return and keeps spamming writes, socket buffer fills. Are we checking write return values and waiting for 'drain' / write-ready?

maria: runtime code uses non-blocking writes and a small batching window. snippet from the streaming loop: 
```
while (!done) {
  chunk = produceChunk();
  socket.write(chunk); // we weren't checking return value here in older branch
}
```
I pushed a local fix that respects the boolean result and awaits 'drain' event if false. but still want to confirm proxies and tcp settings.

pete: also check gzip. gzip turns event-stream into a single compressed stream; proxies often buffer to compress efficiently, eliminating streaming semantics and exacerbating backpressure. for SSE we should disable gzip/deflate and ensure chunked transfer is preserved. nginx config: `proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding ""; proxy_buffering off;`

alex: noted. I also saw entries in our load-balancer logs: 
```
[ALB] 2026-01-24T10:29:18 client=1.2.3.4 target=10.0.2.13 request=req_abc123 status=499 "client closed" bytes_sent=128
```
499 client closed is common when mobile kills the socket while server still writing.

jin: for mitigation: 1) send heartbeat comment lines at shorter interval (eg every 10s) `: keepalive\n\n` to keep upstream proxies and read-side alive. 2) disable gzip for event-streams 3) ensure proxy_buffering off for nginx, `proxy_request_buffering off` if clients send bodies. 4) respect backpressure in runtime and react to 'drain'. 5) add server-side metric for 'stream write stalls' and alert.

alex: adding heartbeat to customer and enabling `proxy_buffering off` on our nginx rotes for /v1/streams/*. will test.

maria: below are repro steps I'm using locally (please run in a linux box):
1) run our runtime locally on :8080 (no proxy).
2) start stream request: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' | pv -L 10`
3) observe runtime logs for EAGAIN within ~10-30s.
4) repeat but run `nginx -> runtime` with `gzip on` and `proxy_buffering on`, you'll see writes stall faster and more 499.

example client JS showing problematic consumer (backgrounded tab will throttle setTimeouts):
```
const es = new EventSource('/v1/streams/generate');
es.onmessage = (e) => {
  // heavy processing that blocks main thread
  doHeavyWork(e.data);
}
```
In mobile webviews this leads to very slow reads, which is a slow consumer.

sam: OS tunables: net.core.wmem_max and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem control send buffer sizes; increasing them can absorb bursts but won't fix slow consumer behaviour long-term. Also ensure keepalive and tcp_user_timeout are reasonable for mobile networks.

pete: another quick workaround: detect slow consumer on connection and switch to smaller chunks/chunk interval so each write is small and less likely to fill socket. also avoid large aggregates per event.

alex: actions I'm taking now: 
- enable heartbeat event every 10s on runtime (temporary)
- turn off gzip for event-stream responses in gateway config
- set proxy_buffering off for streams in nginx 
- patch runtime to honor write backpressure and await drain 
- instrument and create a dashboard for stream write stalls and 499s

maria: sounds good. reminder: if customer uses Cloudflare, CF may buffer and reassemble, and there are CF-specific settings (disable HTTP/2 proxy buffering, or use 'unbuffered' worker). ask CS to confirm CF config.

jin: once fixes deployed, we should run a load test that simulates many slow consumers. script for reproducible load: 
```
# spawn N clients that read slowly
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://lb.internal/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' | pv -L 5 > /dev/null &
done
```
watch our metric `runtime.stream.write_stalls` and ALB 499 count.

pete: also verify node/golang runtime flush APIs: in node `res.flushHeaders()` and `res.write()` + listen for `drain`; in go `flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher); flusher.Flush()` after each write.

alex: deploying patch to staging with heartbeat + backpressure fix. will report back once we run the 200-slow-client test. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment started: runtime @ staging (sha: d4e5f7) by maria.

maria: quick note after deploy to staging: heartbeat visible, gzip disabled for stream route, nginx `proxy_buffering off` applied. initial test with 200 slow clients shows 10x fewer 499s and stalls reduced by ~70% in preliminary runs.

alex: moving customer to staging patch for canary tomorrow and coordinating with their CS contact to test on their mobile fleet.

jin: follow-up checklist for prod rollout: 1) add monitoring alert on `stream.write_stalls_rate` 2) add runbook steps for 499 spike during mobile carrier incidents 3) document SSE config caveats in devex docs.

pete: i'll write the short devex doc explaining: disable gzip, proxy_buffering off, heartbeat interval, backpressure handling patterns.

alex: awesome. closing this thread after prod canary.
